summary: Two blind readers preferred the pre-revision draft, one with high confidence. The revision removed the named register defects but also removed the connective argument, so the concise study now reads as a list of sources. Repair by restoring the argument in plain form, never by restoring the removed ornaments.

findings.problem: The themes pages no longer state the tension the Mass's texts set up: the Gospel's bound prisoner who says his kingdom is not of this world and his servants do not fight, against the chants of universal rule and the Postcommunion's faithful who fight under his standard. The opening describes the propers in order without movement.
findings.required_result: State that tension plainly as what the texts say, early in the section, and let the following units answer it. A plain model: 'Beside the chants the Gospel seems to contradict them: the King who is to rule from sea to sea, adored by all kings, is a bound prisoner who says his servants do not fight for him. Yet the Postcommunion will ask that the faithful fight under his standard.' No 'sharpens every claim', no 'on which the feast turns'.

findings.problem: Plain one-sentence explanations of hard patristic points were cut with the maxims, leaving quotations side by side: Aquinas's 'it is here, because it is everywhere' (the earlier draft explained it: a kingdom whose origin is in one place is bounded by that place, one whose origin is above by none); why the eternal Son asks (God wills that even what is owed be received by asking); Bede's giver and receiver as one Son in two natures.
findings.required_result: Where a quoted Father's point is hard, give one plain sentence explaining it, attributed to him, as a step of the argument (not a closing maxim, chiasmus or restatement).

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex, the kings section and the close
findings.problem: The kings section opens on 'The Fathers and later commentators give the kings three distinct places' with no question for the three places to answer; the earlier draft named it (read alone, the Gospel's denial could empty the Collect's subjection of public consequence, or the Gradual could make Christ a rival to Caesar). The commentary now ends on the senses paragraph without a conclusion.
findings.required_result: Open the kings section with the question in plain form (who holds each misreading, or that the texts invite it). End the commentary with a short comparison that says what each interpretation contributes and how the three meet in the Preface's sentence (the anointing and self-offering; the kingdom of truth; the handing over), as content, not as an 'in one sentence' refrain.

findings.problem: New tics: remarks about the document's own citations ('The writers cited for them disagree on particular verses…', 'Augustine and Hilary are cited in all three', 'The Mass as a whole can be interpreted in three ways.'), and the formula 'Taken this way' / 'Taken together' repeated as a linking phrase.
findings.required_result: State the substance instead of who is cited (what they disagree about, and why it matters to the reading of the Mass). Mark the study's inferences in ordinary, varied words where they are drawn; no fixed formula.

findings.problem: Some details the revision added are unused ('The 1962 Missal prints that verse as the caption of the engraved headpiece above the Mass'), and some paragraph openers are orphaned by cut topic sentences ('The giving that Jerome expounds by Philippians stands in the half of Dan 7:14 that the Alleluia does not sing.').
findings.required_result: Give each added detail its use or cut it; give orphaned openers the plain topic sentence they need. Keep the revision's real gains: the Introit's omitted gifts and clause, the opening of Ps 2, the dilecto Filio link to Col 1:13, the Ps 71 verses the Gradual skips.
